out.rationale: The authors carry the debate-versus-consultancy comparison into the condition Michael et al. leave open (judges with strong priors or biases) and say so explicitly, which is EXTENDS. Their conclusion (p10 L31-L34) reports that debate improves accuracy and calibration over consultancy even with strong priors, but that result is outside this span.

text: The authors cite Michael et al. [36] among work showing debate's effectiveness with unreliable experts, and say prior work largely ignores judges who exhibit cognitive biases or hold strong prior beliefs. They state that their work addresses this by testing whether debate remains effective when judges have such biases about controversial topics, using human judges with varying prior beliefs and LLM judges with and without simulated personas.
title: Rahman et al. extend Michael et al.'s debate-vs-consultancy test to judges with strong prior beliefs
